final_proof:
The claim is false as stated, because the hypotheses do not require f to be surjective.

Indeed, let T₁ be the one-point space {*}, let T₂ = ℚ with the topology inherited from ℝ, and define f(*) = 0. The space T₁ is compact and locally connected, T₂ is Hausdorff, and f is continuous. On the other hand, ℚ is not locally connected. To see this, first note that every connected subset of ℚ has at most one point: if A ⊆ ℚ contained distinct points a < b, choose an irrational number r with a < r < b. Then A ∩ (−∞,r) and A ∩ (r,∞) would be disjoint, nonempty subsets that are open relative to A and whose union is A, contradicting connectedness. Thus the only nonempty connected subsets of ℚ are singletons. No singleton is open in ℚ, so no point of ℚ has a connected open neighborhood. Hence ℚ is not locally connected, which disproves the stated claim.

The natural corrected statement is: the image f(S₁), endowed with the subspace topology inherited from T₂, is locally connected. In particular, if f is surjective, then T₂ is locally connected.

Proof of the corrected statement. Put Y = f(S₁), and regard f as the continuous surjection q: S₁ → Y. We first prove that q is a quotient map. If F is closed in S₁, then F is compact because it is a closed subset of the compact space S₁. Consequently q(F) is compact. The space Y is Hausdorff, being a subspace of the Hausdorff space T₂, and every compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed. Hence q(F) is closed in Y. Thus q is a closed continuous surjection. It follows that q is a quotient map: if A ⊆ Y and q⁻¹(A) is open, then q⁻¹(Y ∖ A) is closed, and therefore q(q⁻¹(Y ∖ A)) = Y ∖ A is closed, where surjectivity was used. Thus A is open.

We next recall directly why components of open sets behave well in a locally connected space. Let G be open in S₁ and let D be a connected component of G. For each x ∈ D, local connectedness supplies a connected open set Vₓ with x ∈ Vₓ ⊆ G. Since D and Vₓ are connected and meet at x, their union is connected. The maximality of D as a connected subset of G therefore gives Vₓ ⊆ D. Hence D is the union of the open sets Vₓ as x ranges over D, so D is open in S₁.

Now let U be any open subset of Y, and let C be a connected component of U. The set q⁻¹(U) is open in S₁. For any x ∈ q⁻¹(C), let Dₓ be the connected component of q⁻¹(U) containing x. By the preceding paragraph, Dₓ is open in S₁. Moreover, q(Dₓ) is a connected subset of U and contains q(x) ∈ C. Since C is the maximal connected subset of U containing q(x), we have q(Dₓ) ⊆ C, and hence Dₓ ⊆ q⁻¹(C). It follows that

q⁻¹(C) = ⋃_{x ∈ q⁻¹(C)} Dₓ,

so q⁻¹(C) is open in S₁. Because q is a quotient map, C is open in Y.

Thus every connected component of every open subset U of Y is open. Given y ∈ U, the component of U containing y is consequently a connected open neighborhood of y contained in U. This is exactly local connectedness. Therefore f(S₁) is locally connected. If f is surjective, then f(S₁) = S₂, and the desired conclusion follows under that additional hypothesis.
